evidence.description: Document add is exercised in the CRUD smoke test on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Named SolrUpdateOptions now expose overwrite, commitWithin, and SolrCloud _route_ serialization; request parameter serialization and invalid values are covered by unit tests. SolrCloud integration tests verify add/update route behavior on an implicit-router collection using shard-scoped query read-back, and verify commitWithin search visibility without a manual commit on the pinned _default configset, across Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. The commitWithin test asserts bounded eventual visibility only; hard/soft commit behavior remains controlled by server configuration. Field-specific SolrAtomicUpdateOperation and SolrAtomicUpdateDocument types plus atomicUpdate() support set, add, add-distinct, remove, removeregex, and numeric inc. Unit, consumer type, and pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 integration tests cover atomic updates. Single JSON documents use /update/json/docs; arrays use /update. Both forms are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. commitWithin is a scheduling hint whose hard/soft behavior is controlled by Solr's commitWithin configuration; the client does not force either commit type. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Unit tests assert the single-document, document-array, and command-map JSON endpoint selection, typed response header, and HTTP error propagation. Unit tests assert single-document, document-array, and command-map endpoint selection, typed response headers, and HTTP error propagation.  Nested parent/child/grandchild JSON document indexing and exact Unicode/multi-valued field read-back are covered by test/integration/solr-document-fidelity.test.ts; these new assertions are pending execution in the pinned standalone CI matrix. Nested documents must be sent using the array form add([document]) so the request uses /update; Solr's /update/json/docs convenience path flattens complex JSON by default. See docs/update.md and ADR 0003. Nested parent/child/grandchild document round-trip and Unicode/multi-valued field round-trip cases have been added to the standalone integration suite; pinned Solr runtime evidence is pending CI.
Field-specific atomic update modifiers are covered by unit/type assertions and integration tests on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

SolrCloud CREATE/LIST/DELETE, alias lifecycle, implicit-router shard lifecycle, named ADDREPLICA/DELETEREPLICA lifecycle, replica property add/delete and BALANCESHARDUNIQUE responses, plus multi-node MOVEREPLICA and REBALANCELEADERS leader reassignment are tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #177, #192, #209, and PR #142 CI #224). MOVEREPLICA verifies the named replica becomes active on a different live node. REBALANCELEADERS assigns preferredLeader to an active non-leader and verifies it becomes shard leader. Distinct snapshot operations and some cluster-state response details remain unverified. The BACKUP/LISTBACKUP/RESTORE/DELETEBACKUP and async status flow described below is integration-tested; this does not certify every snapshot action or response field. Additional operation evidence: Typed SolrCloud collection backup/restore actions and asynchronous REQUESTSTATUS/DELETESTATUS tracking. Full backup, list, restore, query read-back, and delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 with a shared local filesystem volume mounted on both SolrCloud nodes. S3 and other external repositories are not certified. LISTALIASES defaults to SolrCollectionAliasesResponse; CREATEALIAS/DELETEALIAS default to SolrCollectionAliasResponse; CLUSTERSTATUS defaults to SolrClusterStatusResponse with extensible collection/shard/replica models. Filtered cluster status and unobserved version-specific fields remain optional/open. CREATESHARD/DELETESHARD now default to SolrCollectionShardOperationResponse and remain integration-tested on all pinned versions. SPLITSHARD has a typed V1 split.key contract (shard or routing-key mode). MIGRATE uses V1 collection/split.key/target.collection/forward.timeout/async parameters and the same response envelope. Both now have opt-in asynchronous integration checks that require SOLR_DESTRUCTIVE_OPT_IN=true, a loopback endpoint, SOLR_CLOUD=true, SOLR_MULTINODE=true, and disposable collections; the manual workflow provisions its own two-node cluster. The tests verify child-shard state and document read-back after split, and target document read-back after migration. The opt-in workflow has not yet been executed, so both operations remain runtime-unverified. Abort, partial-failure recovery, and concurrent-write behavior are not certified. RELOAD now has exact action-specific serialization and isolated collection integration coverage on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. MODIFYCOLLECTION, ADDROLE, and REMOVEROLE now have dedicated serialization and consumer type fixtures; MODIFYCOLLECTION remains runtime-unverified because it mutates collection policy, while role actions remain runtime-unverified because they mutate cluster-wide node role assignments. Named response contracts now cover every action literal: LIST uses SolrCollectionListResponse; CREATE/DELETE/RELOAD/MODIFYCOLLECTION use SolrCollectionAdminResponse; replica lifecycle, movement, balancing, and property actions use SolrCollectionReplicaResponse; ADDROLE/REMOVEROLE use SolrCollectionRoleResponse. CollectionAdminResponse<A> selects the default contract from the action literal while explicit caller generics remain supported. These are extensible response envelopes, not a claim that all action-specific payload fields or all actions are runtime-certified.

Hard commit with waitSearcher is exercised by the CRUD and update integration tests on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests. SolrCommitOptions expose waitSearcher, softCommit, expungeDeletes (hard-commit only), and openSearcher (request parameter); integration tests cover openSearcher=false and expungeDeletes on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Legacy CommitOptions.maxSegments is deprecated and rejected. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.

Config API set-user-property plus GET /config/overlay userProps read-back pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup unsets the property (CI #166). An isolated temporary request handler is added, read back through GET /config, and removed on all three pinned versions. Common set-property/unset-property names and property-specific values are exported for the shared Solr 8.11/9.11/10.1 baseline. SolrConfigRequestHandlerParams adds value-aware autocomplete for common request defaults/appends/invariants (q, fq, fl, rows, start, sort, wt, echoParams, time limits) while keeping the parameter map open. Effective read models distinguish request handlers, search components, response writers, init params, and listeners; response writers expose contentType/charset and listeners expose standard event names while allowing plugin event strings. Search-component and other plugin-defined options remain open and use customOptions for flattened command-specific extensions. Consumer fixtures cover typed common handler parameters, invalid known values, named read models, existing set-property allow-list, user properties, and config responses. Security API authentication/authorization checks remain in the separate security matrix (CI #162); version-specific common properties remain outside the shared property union.

STATUS has exported CoreAdminStatusResponse with typed per-core paths/config metadata, optional index statistics, initialization failures, and extensible unknown fields. Non-STATUS actions default to exported CoreAdminCommandResponse (responseHeader plus extensible fields); callers can supply a more specific generic. Unit and consumer type fixtures cover minimal/detailed STATUS payloads and non-STATUS response inference. Isolated CREATE, STATUS, and RELOAD pass with unique disposable cores on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup UNLOADs them (CI #145). RENAME, SWAP, MERGEINDEXES, SPLIT, REQUESTSTATUS, and REQUESTRECOVERY are not runtime-certified.

Document deletion by ID is exercised in the CRUD smoke test on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Delete-by-ID and delete-by-query serialization are covered by unit tests; SolrDeleteOptions expose route and commitWithin, with runtime verification of these request options remaining unverified on Solr 8/9/10. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Delete-by-query is integration-tested with persisted-state assertions: all matching documents are removed while a non-matching document remains on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

Typed SolrExportParams requires fl and sort, supports filter query arrays, raw or structured sort expressions, batchSize, response writer selection, optional local expr, and customParams. export() returns the raw backpressure-aware Response. Sort fields must be single-valued docValues int/long/float/double/string fields; fl additionally supports date/boolean and multi-valued fields. includeStoredFields=true is runtime-tested specifically on Solr 10.1.0: the integration test reads back a stored-only field. No runtime support claim is made for Solr 8.11.4 or 9.11.0. The general raw Export response flow is independently tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0; unit tests cover typed serialization.

GET /config reads back an isolated request handler after add and update, and confirms its removal after delete on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. The effective configuration response is asserted, not merely the HTTP status.

GET /config/overlay reads back Config API property mutations and verifies unset cleanup on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. This is persisted overlay state, distinct from effective GET /config.

JVM response-format coverage remains distinct: observed JSON registry on Solr 8/9 and Prometheus exposition on Solr 10.1. A node group check asserts non-empty JSON registry data on Solr 8/9 and Prometheus samples on Solr 10.1. Registry, prefix, and regex filters are asserted against JSON responses on Solr 8/9; Solr 10.1 supports Prometheus/OpenMetrics rather than the JSON writer. Exported SolrMetricsJsonResponse, SolrMetricsRegistry, and SolrMetricValue model stable envelope/value shapes while leaving registry and metric names open for plugins and future Solr versions.

Optimize followed by query asserting committed documents remain available passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments and waitSearcher with unit and consumer type coverage; the existing optimize behavior remains integration-tested on all pinned versions. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments, waitSearcher, and openSearcher; maxSegments is optimize-only and defaults to Solr's unlimited target. The integration test exercises maxSegments on all pinned versions. openSearcher is request-parameter serialized; its optimize-specific runtime effect remains unverified. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.
Ping response status OK is asserted on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145).

Generic SolrResponse<TDocument> and SolrQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> types expose document metadata, classic facet counts, caller-shaped JSON facets, highlighting, grouping, stats, and debug sections. Consumer compile tests verify document inference and response-section property types. Basic query serialization and document retrieval plus cursorMark multi-page traversal are tested on the pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; typed declarations do not certify every optional response section at runtime. Typed classic Facet Component options cover field facets and per-field limit/offset/sort/mincount/missing/prefix/method overrides, query facets, and numeric/date range facets with include/other/hardend and filter/dv methods. Solr date bucketing uses range facets; legacy facet.date parameters were removed in Solr 6. Integration coverage asserts field/query counts and numeric/date range response sections on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed highlighting options cover field selection, highlighter method, snippet/fragment sizing, field matching, alternate fields, phrase and multi-term highlighting, encoders/tags, and per-field overrides. Unit and consumer type tests cover parameter serialization and invalid values; integration tests verify returned snippets on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed Result Grouping options cover group.field, group.func, group.query, per-group limit/offset/sort, group format/main/ngroups/truncate/facet/cache settings; typed grouped response models expose matches, group counts, and per-group document lists. Typed collapse and expand options serialize the Collapsing Query Parser filter and Expand component parameters, with expanded document maps in the response. Standalone integration tests verify field grouping, group sorting, collapse selection, and expansion on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Function grouping and collapse remain subject to Solr's documented distributed/shard-local limitations. Typed Stats Component options support repeated fields, per-field local statistic selection, percentiles, cardinality, tag/key/excludeTags, global stats facets, and calcDistinct. SolrFieldStats response models include nested facet breakdowns, percentiles, and cardinality. Unit and consumer type tests cover encoding and response properties; integration tests verify numeric aggregates, distinct values/counts, cardinality, and category breakdowns on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed MoreLikeThis Search Component options cover field selection, result count, term/document-frequency thresholds, word/token/query-term limits, boosting, query fields, and interesting terms. Unit and consumer type tests cover serialization and response typing; integration tests verify similar-document results on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Geospatial geofilt/bbox filters and geodist sorting are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 using an isolated LatLonPointSpatialField and deterministic nearby/far points; assertions verify inclusion/exclusion and nearest-to-farthest ordering. SpellCheck is an optional server-side component; the client only serializes request options and types its response, and never mutates dictionary or request-handler configuration. SpellCheck-specific integration coverage is pending the pinned Solr matrix. Long query parameter preservation on the current GET contract (no automatic GET-to-POST switching) is unit-tested in test/transport-serialization.test.ts. Nested-document child-transformer and Unicode read-back assertions are in test/integration/solr-document-fidelity.test.ts and await pinned CI execution. Unicode and nested-document query read-back cases are in the standalone integration suite; long query preservation is covered by transport unit tests. No automatic GET-to-POST fallback is implemented. Suggester is modelled as an optional query component because it is attached to a deployment-configured SearchHandler; typed dictionary/query/count/context/build/reload parameters and dictionary/query-keyed responses are covered by unit and consumer type tests. A disposable configured-handler integration test is added; pinned runtime evidence is pending the current feature CI run.

Typed single-ID and multi-ID requests use distinct generic response shapes. The API supports field selection, repeated filter queries, custom Solr parameters, and shared request controls. Unit tests cover URL/query serialization, cancellation propagation, reserved-parameter protection, and invalid ID/filter/field values; consumer type fixtures cover valid and invalid request forms. Integration coverage is added for uncommitted single- and multi-ID read-back; per-version runtime evidence remains unverified until the pinned Solr matrix passes.

JSON Request API query body now has a typed SolrJsonQueryRequest model and recursive JSON Facet API terms/query/range definitions, nested metrics, and domain transformations. SolrJsonQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> exposes caller-typed facet results. Unit and consumer type tests cover nested serialization and invalid discriminators; integration tests verify terms/query/range facets, nested metrics, and excludeTags domain behavior on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Other JSON Request API options remain available through params or the legacy custom-body overload.

Typed V1 ReplicationHandler commands for enablereplication, disablereplication, indexversion, fetchindex, abortfetch, snappull, abort, enablepoll, disablepoll, details, filelist, backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup; replicationFile() returns raw filecontent streams. Live integration coverage on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 covers indexversion, details, filelist, filecontent, leader enable/disable, and a disposable two-core leader/follower fetch using fetchindex with follower query read-back passed the full standalone/security matrix on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 (CI #640). A bounded disposable-core in-progress abort test passes on Solr 9.11.0 and 10.1.0. Solr 8.11.4 is explicitly deferred: repeated CI runs did not expose details.follower.isReplicating=true during a throttled transfer, so the test is skipped for that version and live abort remains unverified there. enablepoll/disablepoll retain unit serialization coverage only. Core-level backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are integration-tested on all three pinned versions. Filelist uses the generation returned by newer Solr indexversion responses and falls back to the legacy indexversion parameter when that field is absent. Additional operation evidence: Core-level ReplicationHandler backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are typed. Backup defaults to the core dataDir; restore status is polled with restorestatus. Full backup/restore/read-back/delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Custom filesystem locations must be permitted by server allowPaths.

Returns raw replication file content as a Response stream; integration coverage requests a listed leader index file and verifies a successful non-empty binary response on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

Generic escape hatch. It does not imply typed support for every Solr endpoint. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction. Generic custom-handler request tests verify repeated query parameter preservation and extensible unknown JSON response fields in test/raw-request.test.ts. Generic custom-handler extensibility, repeated query parameters, and preservation of unknown plugin response fields are covered by raw-request unit tests. Optional `SolrClientConfig.jsonCodec` applies a caller-supplied parser to successful and structured error JSON payloads and a serializer to JSON request bodies. Tests cover exact BigInt round-trip above 2^53-1, normal numbers, decimals, arrays, nested objects, malformed JSON fallback, HTTP errors, and unchanged native defaults. This is client-side behavior and does not carry Solr server-version certification.

Generic raw-response escape hatch using the shared Solr transport. Supports typed methods, query parameters, headers, request bodies, cancellation, timeouts, retry policy, configured validation, and standard Solr error classes. Relative paths and same-origin absolute URLs are supported; cross-origin absolute URLs, embedded credentials, and fragments are rejected before Fetch to prevent credential leakage. String bodies are passed through unchanged when callers supply an explicit Content-Type. Custom endpoint behavior is unverified on Solr 8/9/10 until endpoint-specific integration tests are added. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction. When `requestRaw()` receives a non-string JSON body or an HTTP error response, it uses the configured JSON codec. Explicit string bodies and successful raw response streams bypass parsing/serialization and remain unchanged.

Rollback discards a pending, uncommitted document on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145). Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.

Field, field-type, dynamic-field add/replace/delete and copy-field add/delete commands are unit-tested for exact serialization and integration-tested with responseHeader.status plus schema read-back on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Copy-field replacement is implemented by delete+add because Solr has no native replace-copy-field command. Integration tests verify full schema metadata, name, version, uniqueKey, and similarity response envelopes on all pinned versions. Similarity plugin mutation remains runtime-unverified. The public client implements V1 Schema API routes; Solr 10 V2 routes are not included.

Authentication overloads default to SolrAuthenticationResponse and accept SolrAuthenticationCommand for BasicAuthPlugin set-user, delete-user, and set-property operations, including documented MultiAuthPlugin Basic scheme wrappers for set-user/set-property. BasicAuth configuration exposes hashed credential strings; these must not be logged or treated as plaintext. Authorization has separate SolrAuthorizationResponse/SolrAuthorizationCommand types for RuleBasedAuthorizationPlugin. Custom plugin schemas remain open/unsupported beyond the explicit extension points. Unit serialization and compile-time fixtures cover auth command shapes; existing authenticated read and set-property/read-back integration tests pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. User create/delete mutations are not performed against shared integration security state.

A newly added document becomes searchable after softCommit on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145). Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests. SolrSoftCommitOptions expose waitSearcher/openSearcher; softCommit() now waits for searcher registration by default and is integration-tested for immediate visibility on all pinned versions. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.

Default SolrStreamingExpressionResponse models the JSON result-set envelope and extensible tuple fields; SolrStreamingExpressionErrorTuple describes in-band EXCEPTION tuples. Callers can supply a response or tuple-specific generic shape. Unknown envelope and tuple fields remain accessible. HTTP-level Solr errors continue through the shared typed transport. SolrCloud search is integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Unit tests cover response parsing, in-band error tuples, cancellation during body consumption, and cleanup after body-stream errors. This API parses the complete JSON response and is not an incremental tuple-stream parser.
System info metadata response passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images.

Replacing an existing document and reading back its updated field is tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Atomic updates are integration-tested on all three pinned versions. Typed JSON updateCommands() has its own inventory entry; its add + commit + persisted-document read-back path is integration-tested on all three pinned versions. Named SolrUpdateOptions now expose overwrite, commitWithin, and SolrCloud _route_ serialization; request parameter serialization and invalid values are covered by unit tests. SolrCloud integration tests verify add/update route behavior on an implicit-router collection using shard-scoped query read-back, and verify commitWithin search visibility without a manual commit on the pinned _default configset, across Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. The commitWithin test asserts bounded eventual visibility only; hard/soft commit behavior remains controlled by server configuration. Field-specific SolrAtomicUpdateOperation and SolrAtomicUpdateDocument types plus atomicUpdate() support set, add, add-distinct, remove, removeregex, and numeric inc. Unit, consumer type, and pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 integration tests cover atomic updates. Single JSON documents use /update/json/docs; arrays use /update. Both forms are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. commitWithin is a scheduling hint whose hard/soft behavior is controlled by Solr's commitWithin configuration; the client does not force either commit type. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.

Typed SolrJsonUpdateCommands supports add, delete, commit, optimize, and rollback command objects; command-object serialization and single/array document routing are unit and consumer-type tested. The integration suite independently executes updateCommands() add + commit, delete by ID, delete by query, optimize, and rollback on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Persisted-state assertions verify both delete forms, preservation after optimize, and discard of an uncommitted add after rollback. Commit command options are exercised for searcher visibility. optimize-specific openSearcher behavior remains unverified. openSearcher values in commit/optimize command objects are extracted to the request parameter; conflicting values are rejected. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.
Returns the Export response body as a backpressure-aware ReadableStream of bytes. It delegates to export(), preserving the same request parameters and server compatibility.

Read-only JVM and process properties. Response is intentionally extensible because available properties vary by runtime and deployment; integration tests verify a representative response on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.
Read-only JVM thread diagnostics. Thread detail and response payload vary by JVM; integration tests verify a representative response on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.
Read-only logger configuration and level information. This client method does not mutate logger levels; integration tests verify a representative response on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

Consumes an AsyncIterable<SolrDocument> and emits a valid top-level JSON array through a backpressure-aware Web ReadableStream. Serializes and validates one document at a time, reuses the configured JSON codec and shared request controls, propagates cancellation/producer errors, and disables retries for the non-replayable POST body. Unit tests cover lazy production, framing, empty input, cancellation, producer failure, JSON codec use, and no-retry semantics. A deterministic 250-document pinned Solr integration test has been added; runtime evidence remains pending the fresh CI matrix. Partial ingestion is possible if the source or connection fails after the server has accepted a prefix; the operation is not atomic and does not auto-commit.

records.title: Prepare v4.0 stable release checklist and changelog
records.roadmapContext: ### Separate release gate v4.0 stable publication remains a separate release-owner decision and must not block feature development. Complete the exact release-candidate CI matrix, release notes/migration summary, npm trusted-publisher configuration and provenance verification, and clean npm consumer smoke test before publication. unreleased.content: ### Added - Replace the v3 functional Axios client with a TypeScript-first Fetch-based `SolrClient`, supporting Node.js 20/22/24, ESM and CommonJS, and no required runtime dependencies; keep Zod optional for runtime validation. - Add typed transport configuration for Basic/Bearer authentication, headers, request defaults, retries, timeouts, cancellation, structured HTTP/network/timeout/abort/validation errors, and safe raw/streaming requests. - Add an autocomplete-first Query API covering parser-specific options, filters, sorting, cursorMark pagination, classic and JSON facets, highlighting, grouping, stats, MoreLikeThis, debug/explain, and spatial helpers. - Add typed document update contracts for JSON documents and command objects, atomic updates, update/delete options, commit/soft-commit/optimize behavior, and update response/error envelopes. - Add typed Core Admin, Collections, Schema, Config, Security, Metrics, and System API contracts, with action-specific request models and response shapes for the operations documented in the API reference. - Add Update API unit coverage for JSON endpoint selection, typed success responses, and Solr HTTP failures, plus Solr 8/9/10 delete-by-query persisted-state integration coverage. - Add Solr 8/9/10 integration coverage for Schema API dynamic-field add/replace/delete and copy-field add/delete, including copy-rule replacement via delete+add. - Add unit and Solr 8/9/10 integration coverage for Schema API add, replace, and delete field-type operations, including analyzer, tokenizer, and filter read-back. - Add unit and Solr 8/9/10 integration coverage for Schema API add, replace, and delete field operations, including typed mutation responses and schema read-back. - Add end-to-end v3-to-v4 migration coverage for health checks, document add/replace/delete, and typed query read-back on Solr 8/9/10. - Add typed core-level and SolrCloud collection backup/restore APIs with asynchronous status handling. - Add typed V1 ReplicationHandler commands and raw file-content streaming through `replication()` and `replicationFile()`. - Add typed response contracts for Schema and Config reads, Security authentication/authorization, Metrics, System diagnostics, Core Admin status/async actions, and Collections aliases/cluster status. - Add typed Collections shard lifecycle and MIGRATE operations, including V1 wire-name corrections and explicit runtime-verification boundaries. - Complete typed V1 Collections CREATE options for shard/replica layouts, routing, node placement, aliases, core properties, and legacy Solr 8.11 placement controls; add compile-time and serialization coverage. - Add typed Streaming Expressions JSON envelopes and Export Handler request/sort models; distinguish parsed JSON expressions from raw streamed Export responses. - Harden the public client boundary by keeping transport configuration private and verifying the package-root stable/experimental/internal export decisions. - Verify the packed npm tarball in clean consumers, including ESM/CommonJS runtime imports, TypeScript declarations, optional Zod absence, and prerelease/stable dist-tag policy. ### Documentation - Add a public API reference and machine-readable operation inventory, with consistency checks against package exports and client methods. - Add action-specific Collections API evidence and an explicit public API review, including the stable, generic escape-hatch, and internal export decisions. - Document npm tarball validation, prerelease dist-tag behavior, release rollback, and the manually gated GitHub Actions/npm OIDC trusted-publishing workflow. - Add a Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 Schema API compatibility matrix with explicit V1/V2 scope and unverified similarity plugin behavior. - Add typed Schema API command responses and read-response models for schema metadata, fields, dynamic fields, field types, copy fields, uniqueKey, and similarity. - Add compile-time checks for the documented Update API examples, including atomic update modifiers, JSON update commands, delete options, and commit/optimize semantics. - Expand the v3-to-v4 migration guide with a complete v4 CRUD example and link its compile-time and Solr integration checks. - Clarify Solr 8/9/10 runtime evidence per endpoint and document the remaining unverified query, update-option, and generic transport behaviors. - Expand standalone, authenticated, and SolrCloud integration CI to Node.js 20/22/24 across Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0; document the complete matrix and its successful CI evidence. - Document ReplicationHandler abort lifecycle evidence per Solr version, including the Solr 8.11.4 observability limitation, and keep one-shot fetch verification separate. - Document the opt-in SPLITSHARD/MIGRATE workflow and retain explicit non-certification until a maintainer manually runs it on every pinned Solr version. All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. See [standard-version](https://github.com/conventional-changelog/standard-version) for commit guidelines. ### [3.0.5](https://github.com/vsimko/node-solr-lambda/compare/v3.0.4...v3.0.5) (2023-06-27) ### [3.0.4](https://github.com/vsimko/node-solr-lambda/compare/v3.0.3...v3.0.4) (2020-05-12) ### [3.0.3](https://github.com/vsimko/node-solr-lambda/compare/v3.0.1...v3.0.3) (2020-05-12) ### Bug Fixes * link to types.d.ts mentioned in jsdocs ([c732f02](https://github.com/vsimko/node-solr-lambda/commit/c732f02bdd16a5be414658b4d92bbc46187af3b7))
